title: The High School Reunion (2): The Gang's Revenge

jokes.text: The Gang chanting 'Reunion! Reunion! Smash 'em up!' while pumping themselves up like it's a war rally for a high school reunion
jokes.setup: High school reunions are mildly awkward social occasions
jokes.punchline: The Gang treats it with the intensity of a military operation or gang war
jokes.explanation: A solid cold open gag using the show's core premise: these people treat trivial things with disproportionate gravity. Works because it immediately reestablishes the Gang's pathetic intensity.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Mac realizes fake tickets, calls Adriano 'Ronnie Rat strikes again'

jokes.text: Dennis: 'That's Tim Murphy, the asshole that slept with my prom date.'
jokes.setup: Tim Murphy greets Dennis warmly and introduces his wife, treating them like old friends
jokes.punchline: Dennis's internal monologue immediately brands him 'the asshole that slept with my prom date,' reducing a normal social interaction to Dennis's obsessive grievance
jokes.explanation: Perfect Dennis characterization. The gap between Tim's warmth and Dennis's seething internal monologue is very on-brand. The line is delivered as straight narration, which makes the pettiness funnier.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: my sister, the Aluminum Monster

jokes.text: Mac announces 'Adriano made fake tickets! Those tickets are fake! Ronnie Rat strikes again!' — immediately followed by chaos and Frank getting bit or hurt ('Son of a bitch')
jokes.setup: The Gang arrives at the reunion ready for revenge
jokes.punchline: Within seconds, everything has already gone wrong — fake tickets, Mac exposing them, Frank injured — before the episode even properly starts
jokes.explanation: The Gang's plans falling apart immediately is a reliable structural joke for the show. Functional but not exceptional — the chaos is a bit unclear from dialogue alone.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: I was also on the mountaintop

jokes.text: Dennis: 'Used to be king of the mountaintop. Now I'm sitting alone at a table at my high school reunion with my sister, the Aluminum Monster.'
jokes.setup: Dennis's grandiose self-image as the most popular kid in school
jokes.punchline: The pathetic reality: sitting alone at a table, the only company being his sister who is nicknamed 'the Aluminum Monster'
jokes.explanation: One of the better lines of the episode. The 'king of the mountaintop' grandiosity crashing into 'sitting alone at a table with the Aluminum Monster' is a perfectly constructed deflation. Specific, character-driven, economical. The casual inclusion of 'the Aluminum Monster' as though it's just Dee's title is a great running-gag payoff.

dialogue.speaker: Sweet Dee
dialogue.line: Fatty Magoo! Right? Everybody, Fatty Magoo. Honk!

jokes.text: Dee calls Ingrid a 'Dork' for carrying a clipboard and being on the alumni association, then immediately mocks her gibberish-style when Ingrid explains herself
jokes.setup: Dee and Dennis are sitting alone at a table, embarrassed and desperate to reconnect with the cool kids
jokes.punchline: Dee immediately resorts to childish, mean-spirited mockery of someone who is clearly doing fine in life — exposing Dee's own arrested development
jokes.explanation: Competent cringe comedy. Dee and Dennis's cruelty being immediately pathetic is the show's bread and butter, but this particular exchange doesn't have a sharp enough punchline to elevate it.

jokes.text: Dennis yells 'Fatty Magoo! Right? Everybody, Fatty Magoo. Honk!' — then tries to honk Ingrid like she's still fat
jokes.setup: Dennis and Dee called Ingrid 'Fatty Magoo' in high school as a cruel nickname
jokes.punchline: Dennis tries to honk her as though she still has fat to squeeze — a genuinely disturbing physical violation — delivered with total oblivious confidence
jokes.explanation: The 'honk' detail elevates this from generic bullying callback to something genuinely disturbing and funny. Dennis's complete lack of self-awareness about how insane this behavior is makes it very character-specific. The visual of him trying to honk her and coming up empty is good physical comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: She's not fat anymore. That doesn't really play.

jokes.text: Mac: 'She's not fat anymore. That doesn't really play.' Dennis insists: 'I'll see it on the sides, and I'll see it in the thighs. Still fat to me.'
jokes.setup: Ingrid has clearly lost the weight; Mac points out the nickname no longer applies
jokes.punchline: Dennis doubles down with increasingly absurd reasoning, rhyming his denial ('sides... thighs') in a way that reveals pure delusion
jokes.explanation: The inadvertent rhyme ('sides... thighs') and Mac's straight-man correction make this work. Dennis's refusal to let reality interfere with his cruelty is on-brand and the scene structure is clean.

dialogue.speaker: Sweet Dee
dialogue.line: 'Cause I'll see it on the sides, and I'll see it in the thighs. Still fat to me, still fat to you, Fatty Magoo...

jokes.text: Dennis launches into a full chant — 'Fatty Magoo, Fatty Magoo, Magoo, Magoo...' — escalating until Ingrid just walks away while he continues
jokes.setup: Dennis's initial 'Fatty Magoo' taunt falls flat because Ingrid isn't fat
jokes.punchline: Instead of stopping, Dennis escalates into a solo, increasingly desperate chant while everyone watches in embarrassment, Ingrid eventually just leaves mid-chant
jokes.explanation: This is classic Always Sunny cringe escalation done well. Dennis's refusal to stop — the chant continuing while Ingrid just walks off — captures the show's core joke about characters who can't read social situations and double down into catastrophe. The aftermath ('That seemed pathetic and mean. Yeah, it was.') is a perfect deflation beat. High rewatch value.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: That seemed pathetic and mean.

jokes.text: After the Fatty Magoo chant implodes, Dennis and Dee's mutual post-mortem: 'That felt very forced.' / 'Yeah, 'cause she's so pretty these days.' / 'She looked fantastic.'
jokes.setup: The Fatty Magoo bit completely crashes — Ingrid leaves, the cool kids don't respond, it's just pathetic
jokes.punchline: Dennis and Dee sheepishly admit to each other that she looks great now, with Dennis calling it 'very forced' — a rare moment of self-awareness immediately followed by them pivoting to new plans
jokes.explanation: The deflation after the failed bit is well-executed. The specific observation 'Only kind of works when you're sitting at a table with the cool kids' — meaning the gang used to mock Ingrid WITH social capital and now they have none — is a sharp insight into how their cruelty was predicated on status they no longer possess.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: That felt very forced.

dialogue.speaker: Sweet Dee
dialogue.line: Yeah, 'cause she's so pretty these days.

jokes.text: Dennis: 'I'm gonna bang Tim Murphy's black wife.' — presented as the revenge plan
jokes.setup: The Gang needs a revenge plan against Tim Murphy
jokes.punchline: Dennis's plan is to sleep with Tim's wife — specifically noting her race as though it adds some extra layer of insult — delivered with complete confident certainty
jokes.explanation: Funny primarily through Dennis's confidence and the absurdity of his 'system' — the race detail is the show flagging that Dennis thinks this makes it more of an affront, which is itself a character indictment. Works more as character comedy than as a standalone joke.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: I'm gonna bang Tim Murphy's black wife.

jokes.text: Dee: 'I will bang Tim Murphy to get back at Adriano.' The whole gang: enthusiastic agreement, then Mac: 'The problem is, I don't think Tim Murphy would ever sleep with you.'
jokes.setup: Dee announces her revenge plan — sleep with Tim Murphy — and the Gang is briefly supportive
jokes.punchline: Mac immediately and matter-of-factly says Tim would never sleep with Dee, shutting down the plan without cruelty but with brutal honesty
jokes.explanation: Clean setup/punchline with a good structure — the brief moment of Dee getting support before the rug pull. Mac's flat delivery of the rejection makes it land harder.

dialogue.speaker: Sweet Dee
dialogue.line: I will bang Tim Murphy to get back at Adriano.

jokes.text: Dennis hands Dee two drink tickets as her 'part of the plan' — that's her entire contribution
jokes.setup: Dee asks 'What's my part of the plan?'
jokes.punchline: Dennis silently hands her two drink tickets — her entire role is just to hold the drink tickets while the men pursue their revenge
jokes.explanation: Perfect economy — the entire joke is communicated visually without a word. Dennis's casual dismissal of Dee's value to the group, expressed through the currency of two drink tickets, is both efficient and character-revealing. One of the cleaner visual gags in the episode.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: The problem is, I don't think Tim Murphy would ever sleep with you.

jokes.text: Mac and Charlie hanging from something, Mac: 'The cool kids got us. It was a massacre.'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie went off to execute their part of the plan
jokes.punchline: They're now physically hanging somewhere, describing a social embarrassment as a 'massacre' in the most dramatic possible terms
jokes.explanation: Good visual gag (two grown men hanging somewhere) paired with disproportionate language ('massacre'). Funny but fairly standard for the show's formula.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: 'It was a massacre'

jokes.text: Dee tries to rejoin the cool kids group: 'Look, you guys, I'm on your team, okay? I always was on your team.' They reject her: 'Get away from us.' She calls Cricket a 'goddamn bitch' for blowing her cover
jokes.setup: Dee had apparently tried to infiltrate the cool kids by betraying the Gang
jokes.punchline: The cool kids want nothing to do with her anyway, and she pivots to blaming Cricket with surprising venom
jokes.explanation: Functional cringe comedy but slightly muddy without Part 1 context fully established. The 'You goddamn bitch!' at Cricket is a good button.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: the freight train

jokes.text: Mac describes the 'freight train': 'It was basically just Charlie, Mac, and Dooley. May he rest in peace. God rest his soul.' — a gang member who has died and is briefly mourned
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie propose reassembling their old high school 'gang' called the Freight Train
jokes.punchline: One of the three members is apparently dead, mentioned with a quick 'may he rest in peace' and immediately moved past
jokes.explanation: The casualness of the death mention is the joke — 'may he rest in peace, God rest his soul' rattled off in quick succession and then completely forgotten. Good economy and dark tone fits the show.

dialogue.line: Our conductor's insane. Our cargo is pain. Freight train!

jokes.text: Mac: 'They were basically just lackeys of this guy named Psycho Pete, who genuinely was mentally ill.' Mac and Charlie then recite the Freight Train motto: 'Our conductor's insane. Our cargo is pain. Freight train!'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie's high school 'gang' is being described
jokes.punchline: Their intimidating gang name had a cheesy rhyming motto, led by someone 'genuinely' mentally ill — the gap between their self-image as intimidating and the reality of two dorks with a rhyming catchphrase
jokes.explanation: One of the funnier new concepts introduced in this episode. The motto 'Our conductor's insane / Our cargo is pain' is an inspired piece of writing — it sounds like a tryhard teen's idea of intimidating but is delivered with total sincerity. Highly quotable and reveals the characters perfectly.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: If anything, he'll swoop in at the very end, grab the drunkest girl he can, take her home, bang her. Ha, Schmitty's so cool.

jokes.text: Mac and Charlie realize they don't know Psycho Pete's last name: 'Guess we weren't really that close. It would have been cool to be closer to him.'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are trying to find Psycho Pete's name tag
jokes.punchline: They realize they don't know his last name, then Mac wistfully says it would have been cool to be closer to him — a person who apparently murdered and cannibalized his family
jokes.explanation: The understated wistfulness about not being closer to what will turn out to be a cannibalistic murderer is good dark comedy. The delivery of 'it would have been cool' as genuine regret is well-constructed.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: I've tacked on mass.
Really?

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: I've tacked on lots of mass, yes.

jokes.text: Mac and Charlie see 'Peter Schmidt' on the name list: 'Oh no, that's Schmitty.' Then: 'Schmitty would never come to something like this. Not his scene. If anything, he'll swoop in at the very end, grab the drunkest girl he can, take her home, bang her. Schmitty's so cool.'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are looking for Psycho Pete's name tag
jokes.punchline: They find Schmitty instead — a character who gets his own mythology established, described as effortlessly cool in the most lowbrow way possible. 'Schmitty's so cool' said with genuine admiration
jokes.explanation: Smart setup for a payoff that lands later in the episode. The description of Schmitty's MO is funny on its own but doubles as a plant. 'Schmitty's so cool' said sincerely by these two losers is a great character beat.

dialogue.line: Was he joking when he cut his family into little pieces and ate them for Christmas dinner?

jokes.text: Charlie: 'Not as cool as Adriano.' Mac: 'Way cooler than you, Dirtgrub.'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are comparing Schmitty's coolness to others
jokes.punchline: Mac pivots to insulting Charlie by his old high school nickname 'Dirtgrub' — the cruelty of the reunion context suddenly turned inward
jokes.explanation: Economical and sharp. The casual use of 'Dirtgrub' by Mac — his supposed best friend — without any malice is a great character moment. The Gang is constantly cruel to each other without noticing.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: I specialize in bird law, so I don't want to mess around...

jokes.text: Ingrid returns and Mac tries the 'Fatty Magoo' chant again. Ingrid: 'I'm not fat anymore. That's not even accurate.' Mac: 'Well, you used to be fat.' Ingrid: 'I had a thyroid problem. What's your excuse?' Mac: 'I've tacked on mass. I've tacked on lots of mass, yes.'
jokes.setup: Mac tries the failed Fatty Magoo bit again on Ingrid
jokes.punchline: Ingrid immediately counters with 'What's your excuse?' pointing out Mac's own weight, and Mac's defensive response ('I've tacked on mass') is perfectly in-character for Mac's vanity/denial about his weight
jokes.explanation: One of the best jokes in the episode. This is the kind of multi-layered joke the show does best: Ingrid turns the cruelty back on Mac, Mac's response ('I've tacked on mass') is a perfect expression of his Season 7 weight-denial arc, and the exchange works both as a standalone joke and as deep character payoff. 'I've tacked on mass' is an instantly iconic Mac line. Justified 8+ score — this is comparable to the 8.0 anchor in its specificity, economy, and character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: I'd rather get blasted in the balls by a battering ram than have to have a conversation with the guy.

jokes.text: Mac: 'Was he joking when he cut his family into little pieces and ate them for Christmas dinner?' Ingrid reveals Psycho Pete is the reason they have extra security — he threatened to burn down the building
jokes.setup: Mac is downplaying Psycho Pete's threat to burn down the building as 'his sense of humor'
jokes.punchline: Ingrid reveals Pete murdered and cannibalized his family — specifically 'for Christmas dinner' — delivered as a straight matter-of-fact statement
jokes.explanation: 'Cut his family into little pieces and ate them for Christmas dinner' is a great dark punchline. The specificity of 'for Christmas dinner' is the detail that makes it. Mac's non-reaction ('That doesn't sound like a joke' / 'Psycho is how it sounds') adds a great secondary beat. Strong dark comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Baby's got back, Christie. Baby's got back.

jokes.text: Charlie: 'Although, really I specialize in bird law, so I don't want to mess around...' in the context of discussing Psycho Pete's insanity plea
jokes.setup: The group is discussing whether Psycho Pete's insanity plea was legally sound
jokes.punchline: Charlie, who is functionally illiterate, pipes up to offer legal analysis and then clarifies he 'specializes in bird law' — his recurring delusion that he is a lawyer
jokes.explanation: Bird law is one of the show's best running gags and this deployment is perfect — the dark context (cannibalism/insanity pleas) makes the pivot to bird law even more absurd. The casualness of 'I don't want to mess around' in this specialist capacity is pitch-perfect Charlie. High quotability and rewatch value.

dialogue.speaker: Christie
dialogue.line: Because you're gay.

jokes.text: Mac's reaction: 'That doesn't sound like a joke.' / Charlie: 'Did that really happen?' / Mac: 'Yeah, that sounds much more serious.' / Charlie: 'That's-That's grizzly.'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie have just been told Pete ate his family
jokes.punchline: Their collective reaction is a series of profound understatements — 'That's grizzly' instead of horrified outrage — as they slowly recalibrate their Pete-reverence
jokes.explanation: Charlie's 'That's-That's grizzly' is a malapropism/mispronunciation (he means 'grisly') that's perfectly in character for Charlie. The correction 'Grizzly? Psycho. Psycho is how it sounds.' is a good gag. The understatement is well-played.

dialogue.speaker: Christie
dialogue.line: Dude, you're wearing makeup.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Yeah, I'm wearing a little bit of makeup. Who-who doesn't... And a girdle.

jokes.text: The Gang refuses to let Dee join the Freight Train. Mac: 'The freight train never let a loser down in need. If Dee wants in on the freight train, we have to let her in.' Then: 'Dee just has to do one thing — go through the freight train initiation.'
jokes.setup: Dee wants to join the Freight Train; Mac initially defends her right to join
jokes.punchline: The 'mercy' of letting her in comes with an initiation — which we then see is apparently humiliating/painful given Dee's reaction
jokes.explanation: Setup for the visual gag payoff. The comedic value here is mostly anticipatory. 'The freight train never let a loser down in need' is a funny line in context.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: I was demonstrating value... then I engaged you physically... nurturing your dependence... neglect you emotionally. That's what I do, Christie.

jokes.text: Dee goes through the initiation — screaming 'I am a grown woman! I am a grown woman!' while clearly being physically abused/hazed, with a pop ballad playing
jokes.setup: Dee agreed to the Freight Train initiation to be let in
jokes.punchline: Whatever they do to her causes her to scream 'I am a grown woman!' repeatedly — the contrast between her dignified protest and the indignity of the situation, scored to a romantic pop ballad
jokes.explanation: 'I am a grown woman!' is a great recurring protest line — Dee's dignity being completely destroyed while she asserts it makes for excellent cringe comedy. The pop ballad scoring adds another layer of absurdity. High rewatch value and quotability.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: I am the king of the mountaintop! I reign supreme over everyone in this school. I am the golden god of this place. I reign supreme. I!

jokes.text: Dennis approaches Christie (Tim Murphy's wife): 'Cuff links? Tim, at a high school reunion? It's not the Oscars.'
jokes.setup: Dennis is executing his plan to seduce Tim Murphy's wife as revenge
jokes.punchline: His opening gambit is petty criticism of Tim's fashion choices — establishing Dennis's 'system' by tearing down the competition
jokes.explanation: Decent character beat that establishes Dennis's pickup methodology. Functional but not especially sharp.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: I am the golden god of this place. I reign supreme. I!

jokes.text: Dennis: 'I'd rather get blasted in the balls by a battering ram than have to have a conversation with the guy.'
jokes.setup: Dennis is trash-talking Tim Murphy to Christie to lower her opinion of her husband
jokes.punchline: The extreme specificity and violence of the 'battering ram to the balls' simile, delivered with complete sincerity
jokes.explanation: The specific violence of the image ('battering ram') is the joke. It's an absurdly over-the-top way to say 'boring' and the specificity makes it work. Good quotability.

jokes.text: Dennis: 'Baby's got back, Christie. Baby's got back. You know what I'm saying? Am I right, though? ... I want to be inside you. I want to do shit to you that is gonna make you realize what a worthless, boring piece of shit your husband really is.'
jokes.setup: Dennis has been smoothly gossiping with Christie and pivots to overtly sexual pursuit
jokes.punchline: His 'seduction' speech is completely insane — he talks about her attractiveness, then immediately tells her he wants to make her realize her husband is a 'piece of shit,' which is clearly his true motivation
jokes.explanation: Dennis's combination of genuine sexual aggression and complete transparency about his revenge motivations is pure character comedy. The 'Baby's got back' delivery is unhinged in a great way. The pivot from compliment to 'worthless piece of shit husband' reveals that the seduction is entirely about Tim Murphy, not Christie.

dialogue.speaker: Sweet Dee
dialogue.line: I'm feeling very, very lucky to have my asshole ripped in half like tissue paper by my father and his very good friends.

jokes.text: Christie: 'Wait, I'm confused. Why would you want to have sex with me?' Dennis: 'Why the hell wouldn't I?' Christie: 'Because you're gay.' Dennis: 'What?! I'm not gay.'
jokes.setup: Dennis has been smoothly operating his seduction system
jokes.punchline: Christie flatly says 'because you're gay' — the audience and Christie can see what Dennis cannot: his elaborate system reads as gay behavior
jokes.explanation: Very well-constructed. The setup is Dennis's confidence in his system; the punchline is an outside observer seeing him clearly. Christie's flat delivery of 'because you're gay' is a perfect subversion. Dennis's immediate defensive 'What?! I'm not gay' makes it funnier. This works because it punctures Dennis's self-mythology and because it's accurate.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Tools! Uh, duct tape, zip ties and gloves! I have to have my tools!

jokes.text: Christie: 'Dude, you're wearing makeup.' Dennis: 'Yeah, I'm wearing a little bit of makeup.' Christie: 'And a girdle.' Dennis: 'Yeah, I wanted to seem thin for the occasion. That's not weird.'
jokes.setup: Christie is explaining why she thinks Dennis is gay
jokes.punchline: Each item of evidence (makeup, girdle, gossiping) Dennis defends as normal behavior — the escalation of his denials getting more absurd with each one
jokes.explanation: The escalation of Christie's evidence and Dennis's increasingly elaborate defenses is well-structured. 'I wanted to seem thin for the occasion. That's not weird.' is a great line — said with total conviction while being completely weird. Strong character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: It's fetish, it's fetish shit! I-I-I-I like to bind... I like to be bound.

jokes.text: Christie: 'You've also been gossiping with me for the last 20 minutes.' Dennis: 'I was speeding through the steps. I have a system that...'
jokes.setup: Christie is cataloging why she thinks Dennis is gay
jokes.punchline: Dennis's defense is not 'I wasn't gossiping' but 'I was speeding through the steps' — confirming it was a calculated tactic, which makes it both evidence of his gayness AND his manipulative system
jokes.explanation: Good beat. Dennis's admission that he 'speeds through steps' inadvertently confirms he was gossiping intentionally, which is both funny and troubling. The partial sentence 'I have a system that...' tantalizes us with the full Dennis Reynolds Seduction Methodology.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: No, we don't do the toot-toots...

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: We're a train. Why wouldn't we toot-toot?

jokes.text: Dennis explains his entire DENNIS System to Christie: 'I was demonstrating value on the dance floor... engaged you physically... nurturing your dependence... take you to an empty broom closet... bang the shit out of you. And then I was gonna neglect you emotionally. That's what I do, Christie.'
jokes.setup: Christie has accused Dennis of being gay; Dennis explains he was executing his seduction system
jokes.punchline: The DENNIS System, laid out as a rational, clinical methodology, ending with 'neglect you emotionally' delivered as a feature rather than a bug, concluded with 'That's what I do, Christie'
jokes.explanation: This is the standout joke of the episode. The DENNIS System being explained in real-time to the target — with Dennis apparently unaware that this destroys it — is a perfect expression of his narcissism. 'And then I was gonna neglect you emotionally. That's what I do, Christie.' is an all-timer Dennis line. The clinical detachment from his own sociopathy, the pride in the system, and the blissful obliviousness to how horrifying it sounds all combine for one of the show's best Dennis moments. Justified 8+ — this is on par with or exceeds the 8.0 anchor in character integration and originality.

dialogue.line: You were never that cool to begin with. You would just come around saying weird shit about being a golden god or some other insane crap.

jokes.text: Christie: 'Ew!' Dennis: 'Oh, ew! Yeah, aw, oh, yeah, okay, well, your husband is a liar, how about that, Christie? Stay with a liar!'
jokes.setup: Christie has just been told Dennis's sociopathic plan in full detail
jokes.punchline: Her 'ew' triggers Dennis to drop all pretense and pivot to pure petty grievance about Tim Murphy — the mask falls completely
jokes.explanation: The snap from smooth operator to petulant child when Christie says 'ew' is perfect Dennis. 'Stay with a liar!' as a parting shot reveals the whole seduction was really just about Dennis's grudge. Well-constructed character reveal.

dialogue.speaker: Tim Murphy
dialogue.line: I didn't sleep with your prom date. Ronald McDonald slept with your prom date.

jokes.text: Dennis: 'I am the king of the mountaintop! I reign supreme over everyone in this school. I am the golden god of this place. I reign supreme. I!' — music stops dead as everyone stares
jokes.setup: Dennis has just been fully rejected and humiliated by Christie
jokes.punchline: He erupts into a full delusional proclamation of superiority — 'I AM THE GOLDEN GOD' — in the middle of the reunion, music stopping as everyone stares
jokes.explanation: One of the defining Dennis moments in the show. The music stopping, the entire room going silent, and Dennis mid-breakdown screaming 'I am the golden god of this place. I reign supreme. I!' is a masterpiece of character comedy. The final solitary 'I!' with nothing after it is perfect writing. This is a cultural touchstone for the show and justifies the high score.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: This is mass! Don't make it about my weight!

jokes.text: Dee, now in a back brace (the Aluminum Monster): 'I'm feeling very, very lucky to have my asshole ripped in half like tissue paper by my father and his very good friends.'
jokes.setup: Mac and Charlie are telling Dee she's lucky the initiation wasn't worse
jokes.punchline: Dee's sarcastic enumeration of her 'luck,' including her asshole being 'ripped in half like tissue paper' by her own father
jokes.explanation: 'Ripped in half like tissue paper by my father' is a great dark line — the specificity of 'tissue paper,' the casual reference to her father participating, and her sarcastic delivery of 'very, very lucky' all work together. Strong and quotable.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: If you're dealt a bunch of lemons, you got to take those lemons and stuff them down somebody's throat until they see yellow.

jokes.text: Dee, still in the back brace with the Aluminum Monster look: 'And I'm feeling incredibly lucky to be making another appearance as the Aluminum Monster after so many years.' Beat. 'Thank you, thank you.'
jokes.setup: Dee is cataloguing her humiliations from the evening
jokes.punchline: She takes a mock bow for 'another appearance as the Aluminum Monster,' treating her humiliation as a performance with a small ironic curtain call
jokes.explanation: The 'thank you, thank you' after the Aluminum Monster line is a lovely absurdist button — Dee taking a bow for her own degradation. Good character moment and effective callback payoff.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Frank's incoherent motivational speech about lemons

jokes.text: Dennis runs back: 'I am the king of the minions, not Tim Murphy! He... jerk-off idiot!' then demands his fetish tools from his car: duct tape, zip ties, gloves
jokes.setup: Dennis has just had his golden god meltdown; he comes back to rejoin the Gang in full breakdown mode
jokes.punchline: His revenge plan apparently involves fetish tools he keeps in a hidden compartment in his car
jokes.explanation: The reveal of a hidden compartment full of zip ties, duct tape, and gloves is a great dark joke — the implication being that Dennis is a possible serial killer, which is a long-running show subtext. 'Jerk-off idiot' as an insult is also funny in its incoherence.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Well, the thing of it is, is that, uh, there's the lemon stuff. Right. And then you got Mac, who's a rat. And Dee's body brace. And, uh, and that's the thing of it, and... It's good.

jokes.text: Dennis opens the hidden compartment in his car and pulls out duct tape, zip ties and gloves
jokes.setup: Dennis runs to his car in a rage to get 'tools'
jokes.punchline: The 'tools' are duct tape, zip ties, and gloves — classic serial killer/kidnapper supplies — casually kept in a hidden compartment in his car
jokes.explanation: One of the great Dennis Reynolds moments. The hidden compartment alone is alarming. The specific inventory — duct tape, zip ties, gloves — is the classic serial killer kit, deployed with complete matter-of-factness. The gang's reaction ('Well, why do you have a bunch of, like, weird tools in a hidden compartment in your car?') is the audience surrogate. This deepens Dennis's established menace in the show's mythology. High marks for character integration because only Dennis Reynolds has a secret murder kit in his car.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Plan B is a dance routine. It's a goddamned dance routine.

jokes.text: Mac: 'Why do you have a bunch of weird tools in a hidden compartment in your car?' Dennis: 'It's fetish shit! I-I-I like to bind... I like to be bound.'
jokes.setup: Dennis has retrieved zip ties, duct tape, and gloves from a hidden compartment in his car
jokes.punchline: His explanation — it's 'fetish shit,' he likes to be bound — is both a plausible deflection and possibly true, but either way more disturbing than the alternative
jokes.explanation: One of the best jokes in the episode. The hidden compartment with serial killer tools is already funny; Dennis's explanation ('It's fetish shit! I like to be bound!') makes it even better because it simultaneously explains it and doesn't. The stammering delivery ('I-I-I like to bind... I like to be BOUND') suggests he's making it up on the spot. The show has always hinted Dennis might be a serial killer; this is a perfect expression of that joke. Justified 8+ — high originality, perfect character integration, economical.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: That's how they solved their problems-- through dance. Then, all of a sudden, we stopped dancing... Then, later on, kids wore trench coats and shot each other in school, and that's not cool.

jokes.text: Dennis: 'That's not important! There has to be questions! I'm not taking questions! The golden god is not taking questions!'
jokes.setup: Mac and others are questioning Dennis about his tools
jokes.punchline: Dennis refers to himself in the third person as 'the golden god' while refusing to answer questions about his fetish murder kit
jokes.explanation: Third-person golden god reference in this context is funny. The refusal to take questions about his possible serial killer tools is good Dennis characterization.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: They also give each other blow jobs. They got these things called rainbow parties.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: No, Charlie.

jokes.text: Mac declares Dennis the new Psycho Pete: 'You're gonna be our new Psycho Pete, pal.' Everyone gets hyped for the Freight Train with chanting, then someone tries 'choo-choo' and Mac shuts it down: 'No, we don't do the toot-toots.' 'Why wouldn't we toot-toot?' 'It's just not what we do, okay?'
jokes.setup: The Gang rallies for the Freight Train with Dennis as their new Psycho Pete
jokes.punchline: The momentum of the rally is broken by an argument about whether the Freight Train does toot-toots — Mac's serious insistence that they don't undercuts any intimidation
jokes.explanation: The toot-toot argument is a great absurdist beat — Mac's hyper-specific gang rules being argued in the middle of a war rally. 'It's just not what we do' said with total conviction is very funny. High quotability.

jokes.text: The Freight Train charges back into the reunion with chanting, then argument about whether trains go 'toot-toot': 'No, we don't do the toot-toots.' / 'We're a train. Why wouldn't we toot-toot?'
jokes.setup: The Freight Train is making its dramatic charge into the reunion
jokes.punchline: Mid-charge, they pause to have a earnest argument about whether the Freight Train makes toot-toot sounds — Mac is very specific that they don't do toot-toots — a ridiculous procedural dispute in the middle of a 'battle charge'
jokes.explanation: Classic Sunny gang-dispute comedy. The commitment to procedural accuracy about their own stupid gang lore — specifically 'no toot-toots' — while in the middle of a dramatic charge is a great structural joke. It deflates the moment and reveals that even their rebellion is chaotic and disorganized.

jokes.text: The cool kids' reaction to the Freight Train: 'What the hell are you guys talking about?' Then: 'We're in our 30s. We don't fight people anymore. It's kind of pathetic.'
jokes.setup: The Gang arrives ready for a confrontation, Dennis demanding Murphy come out
jokes.punchline: The cool kids are completely unbothered and just point out the Gang is in their 30s — the most deflating possible response to attempted intimidation
jokes.explanation: The reality check from the cool kids — 'we're in our 30s, we don't fight people' — is a great structural deflation of the Gang's entire episode arc. The normalcy of the antagonists makes the Gang's behavior even more pathetic and funny.

dialogue.line: Tim's after party invitation excluding them

jokes.text: Dennis's big confrontation speech reveals Tim Murphy didn't sleep with his prom date — Ronnie the Rat did. Tim: 'Ronald McDonald slept with your prom date. Did he tell you that I slept with her?'
jokes.setup: Dennis's entire motivation for the reunion is revenge on Tim for sleeping with his prom date
jokes.punchline: Tim didn't do it — Ronnie the Rat did, and apparently told Dennis it was Tim. The entire episode's premise is based on bad information
jokes.explanation: A satisfying structural payoff — the entire two-episode arc's inciting grievance is revealed to be based on a lie from Ronnie the Rat. The Gang's whole plan was built on false information. 'Ronald McDonald slept with your prom date' using Ronnie's full nickname is a good detail.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: I don't understand how that didn't blow people's minds, though.

jokes.text: Mac to the cool kids, mock-crying: (all mock crying) in response to Tim saying they're afraid
jokes.setup: Tim suggests they won't fight because they're scared
jokes.punchline: The Freight Train's response to being called afraid is collectively doing baby-cry mockery — an extremely juvenile taunt that underscores Tim's point about their arrested development
jokes.explanation: Functional gag. The irony of using a baby-cry taunt in a confrontation that was supposed to prove their maturity is there, but the execution is lazy — it's just described as '(all mock crying)' and doesn't have enough specificity to be a great joke.

dialogue.speaker: Sweet Dee
dialogue.line: I'm gonna bang the next person who talks to me. So who's it gonna be?

jokes.text: Tim: 'I never would have slept with that chick. She was gross.' (quietly) Dennis: 'She was gross.' 'She was really gross.' Then Charlie: 'You slept with my prom date?' Mac: 'No... Yes.'
jokes.setup: Tim reveals he would never sleep with Dennis's prom date because 'she was gross'
jokes.punchline: Dennis quietly agrees ('she was gross'), then it comes out Mac slept with Charlie's prom date — a second betrayal revelation landing immediately after the first
jokes.explanation: Double revelation structure is excellent. Dennis's immediate quiet agreement that his prom date was 'gross' is funny on its own. Then the pivot to Mac having slept with Charlie's prom date — 'No... Yes' — lands with an escalating gut punch. The Gang's betrayals of each other are a core comedic engine and this uses it well.

dialogue.speaker: Sweet Dee
dialogue.line: Hey, Schmitty, excuse me. How you doing, having fun?

dialogue.speaker: Sweet Dee
dialogue.line: Oh, do you want to have sex with me?

dialogue.speaker: Schmitty
dialogue.line: Yes, I do.

dialogue.speaker: Sweet Dee
dialogue.line: Well, there you go.

jokes.text: Tim: 'You were never that cool to begin with. You would just come around saying weird shit about being a golden god or some other insane crap. And referring to all of us as your minions.'
jokes.setup: Dennis claims Tim destroyed his social status
jokes.punchline: Tim delivers a flat, evidence-based rebuttal: Dennis was always like this — calling people his minions, claiming to be a golden god — which means Dennis was never cool, he was always just unhinged
jokes.explanation: Tim Murphy serves as the audience's avatar here — the voice of reason confirming what we already know: Dennis has always been delusional. The fact that Dennis's high school behavior was identical to his current behavior (calling people minions, golden god proclamations) makes his arrested development explicit. Very clean structural payoff.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Swooped in and grabbed the most disgusting girl here.

jokes.text: Mac: 'It was very easy. Uh, she was a whore.' Charlie: 'I'm gonna kill you!' Dennis: 'I know she was a whore, but she was my whore!' — accidentally admitting his own prom date was a whore
jokes.setup: Charlie is furious at Mac for sleeping with his prom date
jokes.punchline: Dennis accidentally confirms his own prom date was a whore in the process of defending his proprietary claim to her — 'I know she was a whore, but she was MY whore!'
jokes.explanation: One of the best lines of the episode. 'I know she was a whore, but she was MY whore!' is brilliantly constructed — Dennis is defending his honor while accidentally confirming the insult. The possessive outrage ('MY whore') is a perfect expression of Dennis's self-contradictory character. Highly quotable, great structure, economical. Justified 8+ score.

jokes.text: Mac: 'This is mass!' Charlie: 'Don't make it about my weight!'
jokes.setup: Charlie is angry at Mac; Mac tries to defend himself by pointing to his physique
jokes.punchline: Mac's weight/mass delusion from earlier in the episode comes back — 'This is mass!' — and Charlie's response ('Don't make it about my weight!') misinterprets it as an attack
jokes.explanation: Perfect callback payoff. Mac using 'mass' as a flex during a fight, and Charlie interpreting it as a fat joke about himself (suggesting Charlie may also be insecure about weight), is a compressed and brilliant two-line exchange. The misunderstanding that escalates the fight is classic sitcom structure elevated by character specificity. Among the best-constructed jokes in the episode. Fully justified 8+.

jokes.text: Frank's speech: 'If you're dealt a bunch of lemons, you got to take those lemons and stuff them down somebody's throat until they see yellow.'
jokes.setup: The Gang is demoralized and wants to give up; Frank gives a motivational speech
jokes.punchline: Frank's version of 'make lemonade' becomes an act of violence — 'stuff them down somebody's throat until they see yellow' — delivered as wisdom
jokes.explanation: One of the best lines in the episode. Frank's subversion of the 'when life gives you lemons' cliché into an act of assault is inspired. The specificity of 'until they see yellow' is what makes it exceptional — it's not just violent, it's violently specific. Economical, quotable, perfectly in-character for Frank, and genuinely clever as a joke structure. Justified 8+ — comparable to or exceeding the 8.0 anchor.

jokes.text: Frank's speech loses all coherence: 'Well, the thing of it is, is that, uh, there's the lemon stuff. And then you got Mac, who's a rat. And Dee's body brace. And, uh, and that's the thing of it, and... It's good.' Then: 'I lost my train of thought. Let's go back to the bar.'
jokes.setup: Frank's inspirational speech peaked at the lemon line; the Gang asks what the plan is
jokes.punchline: Frank's follow-through completely disintegrates into half-sentences about Mac being a rat and Dee's brace, before he admits 'I lost my train of thought. Let's go back to the bar.'
jokes.explanation: The collapse of Frank's speech from inspirational peak to incoherent mumbling is a perfect Frank joke. The Gang's moment of genuine emotional investment being deflated by 'I lost my train of thought. Let's go back to the bar.' is structurally excellent. Frank's chaotic ADD is the joke and it works beautifully as a contrast with the previous line.

jokes.text: Frank immediately loses the thread of his own speech: 'Well, the thing of it is, is that, uh, there's the lemon stuff. Right. And then you got Mac, who's a rat. And Dee's body brace. And, uh, and that's the thing of it, and... It's good.'
jokes.setup: The gang asks Frank what the actual plan is after his inspiring speech
jokes.punchline: Frank cannot explain the plan — his 'inspiration' was totally content-free; he trails off listing unrelated things ('Mac, who's a rat,' 'Dee's body brace') and concludes with 'It's good.'
jokes.explanation: Perfect structural payoff to the inspirational speech setup. Frank's speech had great delivery and no content — the reveal that he has no plan is a classic Sunny Frank joke. 'Mac, who's a rat' and 'Dee's body brace' as his attempts to construct a plan are wonderfully random. The fade to 'It's good' is a great button. Frank's confused ramblings being taken seriously then immediately revealed as empty is a cornerstone Frank joke.

jokes.text: The Gang builds to a crescendo about 'Plan B,' whispering it like a covert CIA operation. Dennis: 'Will you stop whispering plan B like it's some super covert CIA operation? Plan B is a dance routine.'
jokes.setup: The Gang builds enormous tension and secrecy around 'Plan B,' treating it like a dangerous covert operation
jokes.punchline: Plan B is a choreographed dance routine — the most anticlimactic possible reveal
jokes.explanation: Perfect misdirection/setup-punchline structure. The extended buildup — whispering, excitement, gravity — makes the reveal ('Plan B is a dance routine') land with maximum impact. Dennis's exasperated delivery of the reveal is great. This is the kind of structural comedy the show excels at. Justified 8+ score.

jokes.text: Frank adds: 'And it's gonna rock.' — beat — after Dennis has already deflated Plan B as a dance routine
jokes.setup: Dennis has just deflated Plan B as 'a goddamned dance routine'
jokes.punchline: Frank's completely sincere, unironic 'And it's gonna rock' — delivered with full confidence — is the perfect button
jokes.explanation: Four words, maximum comedy. Frank's sincere endorsement of the dance routine immediately after Dennis's deflation is a perfect button joke. Economy at its best.

jokes.text: Mac's speech about dance: 'Back in the '50s and the '60s and the '70s, people used to dance all the time. That's the way we solved our problems back then. Then, all of a sudden, we stopped dancing. Grunge came in... kids wore trench coats and shot each other in school.'
jokes.setup: Mac is introducing the dance routine to the reunion crowd
jokes.punchline: Mac's speech connects 'stopping dancing' to grunge, oversized jeans, school shootings — presented as a coherent cause-and-effect historical analysis
jokes.explanation: Mac's pseudo-intellectual social commentary connecting grunge fashion to school shootings to the healing power of dance is inspired absurdism. The logic is completely insane but delivered with total sincerity. The trench coat/school shooting pivot is very dark and very funny.

jokes.text: Frank's speech about the history of dance as social problem-solving, culminating in 'Then, later on, kids wore trench coats and shot each other in school, and that's not cool.'
jokes.setup: Frank is addressing the reunion crowd to introduce Plan B (the dance routine)
jokes.punchline: Frank's history of dance pivots through the '50s-'70s to 'grunge came in, we dressed in plaid' to '...kids wore trench coats and shot each other in school, and that's not cool' — Columbine as a consequence of not dancing enough
jokes.explanation: Very Sunny dark comedy. The logic is insane — that the absence of organized dancing led directly to school shootings — but Frank delivers it with such conviction that it has its own horrible coherence. The 'and that's not cool' understatement after school shootings is good dark comedy execution.

jokes.text: Mac: 'Kids are dancing again. Organized choreographed dance. They're doing organized choreographed dances to solve their problems.' Charlie: 'They also give each other blow jobs. They got these things called rainbow parties.' Mac: 'No, Charlie.'
jokes.setup: Mac is building to an inspirational conclusion about kids dancing
jokes.punchline: Charlie derails the speech by bringing up 'rainbow parties' as another feature of modern youth culture — with equal enthusiasm — and Mac shuts him down with a flat 'No, Charlie'
jokes.explanation: Charlie's sincere, enthusiastic pivot to 'they also give each other blow jobs' as an equivalent positive development in youth culture is perfect character comedy. The 'No, Charlie' is a perfect Mac line — not shocked, just wearily correcting. The specificity of 'rainbow parties' (a real early-2000s moral panic) makes it funnier and more specific. Well above average for the episode.

jokes.text: The Gang's choreographed dance routine — performed to a full song with the whole crowd watching, lights, music, the works
jokes.setup: Plan B is a 'goddamned dance routine' that is apparently going to 'rock'
jokes.punchline: The Gang actually performs a full, committed choreographed dance — the extended visual comedy of five terrible, awkward adults doing a synchronized routine to a crowd
jokes.explanation: The extended dance sequence is a visual comedy set piece that earns its length through the absurdity of the Gang's sincerity and the sheer commitment. Frank vomiting at the end is the button. High rewatch value as a physical comedy moment, though quotability is low since it's primarily visual.

jokes.text: Frank vomits at the end of the dance routine. 'It's fine, it's fine.'
jokes.setup: The dance routine ends on a climactic beat
jokes.punchline: Frank immediately vomits; someone says 'it's fine, it's fine' — the standard Always Sunny acknowledgment that everything is awful
jokes.explanation: Frank vomiting as a button to the dance sequence is a reliable gross-out that fits the character. 'It's fine, it's fine' is a good deflation line. Functional but not exceptional.

jokes.text: 'Well, that was weird.' Then the cool kid: 'Hey, everyone! After party back at my house. Everyone's invited. Except them.' — pointing at the Gang
jokes.setup: The Gang has just performed their dance routine expecting it to win the crowd over
jokes.punchline: The host invites everyone to the after party — with a pointed 'except them' aimed at the Gang — confirming total failure
jokes.explanation: 'Everyone's invited. Except them.' is a great punchline — the specificity of naming them out as the exception makes the exclusion pointed and funny. Perfect structural deflation of the dance sequence.

jokes.text: Post-dance debrief: 'It was a perfect dance. They just didn't respond to it.' / 'I don't understand how that didn't blow people's minds.'
jokes.setup: The dance routine completely failed to impress the crowd
jokes.punchline: The Gang's post-mortem is complete denial — 'it was a perfect dance,' the problem was the audience not appreciating it
jokes.explanation: The Gang's inability to process failure is a core character trait and this is a clean expression of it. 'Those people are stupid. They're idiots, they're savages. They just didn't get it.' is a good line.

jokes.text: Post-dance gang debrief: 'That sucked.' / 'It was a perfect dance. They just didn't respond to it.' / 'I don't understand how that didn't blow people's minds.'
jokes.setup: The dance has failed to achieve revenge or social acceptance
jokes.punchline: Mac and Charlie genuinely cannot understand why a perfect dance didn't 'blow people's minds' — their total inability to process failure through any lens other than the audience's fault
jokes.explanation: Good running character joke. Mac and Charlie's inability to accept failure — specifically blaming the audience for not appreciating their 'perfect dance' — is a great character beat. The gap between 'that sucked' (Frank's direct assessment) and Mac's 'it was a perfect dance' captures the gang's fractured reality-testing.

jokes.text: Dee, drunk and slurring: 'You know what? Just like you low-life shits, I didn't get invited to the after party either, but whatever. I'm just gonna have sex with somebody to feel better about myself. I'm gonna bang the next person who talks to me.'
jokes.setup: Everyone has been excluded from the after party
jokes.punchline: Dee's response is to announce she'll 'bang the next person who talks to me' — a setup that the audience immediately knows will end badly given the show
jokes.explanation: Perfect plant for the Schmitty payoff. Dee's drunk logic ('I'll bang the next person who talks to me') combined with her sloppy delivery is good character comedy and sets up the final joke precisely.

jokes.text: Schmitty walks in exactly as predicted — 'at the very end' of the party — immediately propositions Dee after her announcement. Dee: 'Do you want to have sex with me?' Schmitty: 'Yes, I do.' They leave together.
jokes.setup: Schmitty was described earlier as someone who 'swoops in at the very end, grabs the drunkest girl, takes her home'
jokes.punchline: He appears exactly on cue and executes this plan to perfection — with Dee, who has just announced she'll sleep with the next person who talks to her, being the drunkest person there
jokes.explanation: The best structural joke in the episode. The Schmitty setup from the middle of the episode is paid off with absolute precision — he appears at the exact right moment, targeting the drunkest girl, which is Dee, who has just made a proclamation that makes her a perfect target. Two plants (Schmitty's MO, Dee's announcement) land simultaneously. The Gang's reaction — 'Monster. Schmitty. Swooped in and grabbed the most disgusting girl here.' — is a perfect final button. Justified 8+ — this is genuine craft in comedic construction.

jokes.text: The Gang watching Dee leave with Schmitty: 'Monster.' Then: 'Schmitty just... Schmitty. Swooped in and grabbed the most disgusting girl here.'
jokes.setup: Schmitty has just executed his plan perfectly, leaving with Dee
jokes.punchline: The Gang's reaction is begrudging, almost admiring acknowledgment of Schmitty's cold efficiency — 'Monster' said with a mix of horror and respect — followed by the clinical description 'grabbed the most disgusting girl here' (meaning Dee, their own friend)
jokes.explanation: Perfect button for the episode. 'Monster.' as a one-word reaction is loaded with admiration and horror. The Gang casually referring to their own friend Dee as 'the most disgusting girl here' without any self-awareness is a great final character note. Economical and funny.

tmdb_overview: The gang come up with a new plan to buff their tarnished high-school reputations at their reunion.
